title: The Lordship of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The lordship of Christ means that Jesus is Lord over all. He has divine authority to save, command, rule, judge, forgive, and claim the whole life of every person who follows Him.
summary: The lordship of Christ means that Jesus is Lord over all. He has divine authority to save, command, rule, judge, forgive, and claim the whole life of every person who follows Him.
christFocus: Jesus is the risen Lord whom God has exalted above all. His lordship is not an optional addition to salvation; it is part of who He is as Savior, King, and Christ.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture declares that Jesus is Lord. His resurrection and exaltation reveal His authority over life, death, the church, and every power. Every knee will bow and every tongue confess His lordship.

The lordship of Christ is personal and comprehensive. He does not merely offer help while leaving people in control of themselves. He calls disciples to hear His Word and do what He commands.

Confessing Jesus as Lord is central to faith. This does not mean believers earn salvation by perfect obedience, but true faith receives Christ as He is, not as a Savior separated from His authority.

His lordship is also good news. The One who rules is the One who died and rose for His people. His commands are not tyranny; they are the authority of the Savior who leads His people into life.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
A Christ without lordship allows people to use His name while continuing in self-rule. Scripture will not allow Jesus to be treated as a religious accessory.

This doctrine confronts shallow profession and comforts surrendered believers. The Lord who commands also forgives, restores, strengthens, and keeps those who belong to Him.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Confess Jesus as Lord with your mouth and your life. Bring your choices, desires, habits, relationships, money, ministry, and future under His authority. Where you have resisted His rule, repent and return to Him in faith.
